Part 1. Sketchpad today

1.1 The pieces and how they connect

Sketchpad today is six tabs over a shared pool of memory. Each tab reads and writes two shared state objects, uiState and drawState. Under them sit three kinds of drawing code:

  • the 14 Draw registry objects;
  • the Figures code, which arranges registry objects as layers;
  • the script runner, which runs the pattern and gallery scripts.
All three end in the same place: the drawing helpers in draw/ and classes/, which finish in drawLine, which paints onto the canvas. A separate Node program does every file write and keeps the manifests (the lists of what is in each folder) up to date.

[[FIG v1_map | Sketchpad today: six tabs over shared memory, three kinds of drawing code, one canvas]]

1.2 How a drawing gets onto the screen

Take the Parabola in the Draw tab. Its settings live in params: the four arm ends, the step count, the colour, and also points[0..5], a second copy of the end points that the drag code uses. When you move a slider or drag a red dot, update() compares the copies to work out which point you moved, rebuilds its live objects (a Line and a StringThing), and draw() calls the helpers, which call drawLine once per stitch.

Two things in Figure 2 matter for what follows. The first is that the stitches never exist as a list anywhere: each one is computed and painted in the same moment, inside drawLine. The second is that when Phase 7d needed to know where discs could go, the only way was to add infrastructure(), a second description of the same shape, which has to be kept in agreement with draw() by hand.

[[FIG v1_drawing | One drawing, today: settings, a guess, live objects, and painting]]

1.3 How Figures holds layers and welds

A figure today is an array of layers plus a parallel array of live objects, one per layer. Each layer's object keeps its own copy of its handle positions. A weld is a list of discs that ought to sit at the same spot. Because each layer holds its own copy of that spot, a drag on one layer has to be followed by work to bring the others along, as Figure 3 shows. That work is the propagation walk: four special cases, plus conflicts refused partway through a drag.
